answer: Each identity locks 70 credits in the grove ledger for one unclaimed canyon segment. It files key-signed before-and-after hashes; an inlet auditor replays them against the canyon survey before releasing the bond. Harder segments come later, so fake k pays 100+4(k-1): 70 bond plus 30+4(k-1) work; fake 1,000 pays 4,096, and 1,000 fakes pay 2,098,000. One honest operator clears a segment for 100 and gets 70 back after one clean epoch. Rented clearance fails at the inlet check: a rented hash already sits in the grove ledger, so it is rejected and the bond burns.
